agent_priors_used: PRIOR (general caching-systems knowledge, not SPIDER evidence): a cache or compiled artifact pays for itself only when the reuse count exceeds a break-even that depends on the cost of RE-VALIDATING the cached item, not of producing it. Systems that re-validate cheaply amortize; systems that must re-derive do not. Used to judge that SPIDER's 48.00-versus-38.6 cost separation is a statement about the ledger's re-derivation price as much as about memory.

PRIOR (general tool-agent knowledge, not SPIDER evidence): in long-horizon tool use the dominant failure mode is compounding error across steps, so mechanisms that remove steps compound in value - but a mechanism that silently replays a wrong action injects error at the same rate it removes work. Used to weight the synthetic 80 false compiled replays as an architectural liability rather than a bookkeeping detail, and to justify requiring a null arm that omits gating identity on any replay mechanism.

PRIOR (general measurement knowledge, not SPIDER evidence): an instrument used to adjudicate a cost or economics question must first be calibrated on cases whose correct answer is known by construction, and a battery of constant statistics calibrates nothing. Used to accept physics' diagnosis of its own frozen accept branch and to reject any third certification cycle that repeats it.

PRIOR (general research-system knowledge, not SPIDER evidence): capability that exists only in an uncommitted working tree across many experiment cycles has near-zero expected value, and re-measuring against a moving artifact produces incomparable numbers. Used to make durable commitment at HEAD a binding precondition of the product mandate rather than an auxiliary check.

PRIOR (general research knowledge about fast-moving fields, not SPIDER evidence): external numeric comparators are frequently absent, and an honest, bounded 'no comparator exists' produced cheaply is itself decision-grade because it stops the program spending cycles trying to match a phantom. Used to authorise intel's external-transfer question with a negative as a first-class outcome.

PRIOR (general knowledge about experimental design, not SPIDER evidence): the cheapest sufficient substrate should be preferred until a question genuinely requires a more expensive one. Plain credential-free public HTTP has now been shown inside SPIDER to support 155 real observations with paired bootstrap CIs, so questions about architectural preconditions should be moved onto it before anyone pays for a browser or a model key. Used to put frontier's mandate on real sites with no browser, docker or model key.

PRIOR (general knowledge about human and agentic computer use, not SPIDER evidence - asserted here only as a question, and explicitly handed to intel to measure rather than to assume): the delegable or recurrent fraction of activity in computer use is a minority, not a majority, and the overhead ratio paid for re-deriving that minority is large. The Scout supplied concrete figures for this (R = 60-343x, delegable recurrence h = 7.7-9 percent) from a source SPIDER has never verified. If true, h would bound the entire reachable economic share of SPIDER's product regardless of how good inheritance is, which is why I directed intel to verify or refute it rather than treating it as background.

PRIOR (general knowledge about measurement and research operations, not SPIDER evidence): when a local result is negative-leaning, the first question is whether the instrument or the ledger is at fault before generalising, and the second is to search for the setting in which the mechanism could still win. Used to require product to declare one cost basis and one break-even derivation, and to keep the amortization question alive on a substrate with genuine cold-discovery cost instead of abandoning it on a substrate with none.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: Against continuing the census-acquisition loop: five or more cycles have been spent on WebGym and WebArena manifests and the Codex records HF_TOKEN scope/quota/mirror as an unresolved provisioning block, so the expected yield of a sixth attempt is low and the brief's contrary claim that WebGym is available infrastructure is contradicted by the lane's own accepted evidence. Against the alternative of deploying WebArena-Infinity as a live testbed: even if it deployed, a self-hosted 19-app suite produces a census, not an external comparator, and it does not answer the question of whether a published holdout transfer rate exists. Against spending the cycle on the compiler baselines: audited as over-claimed with a crossed name-to-artifact mapping and one of five targets never located, so a second pass has low marginal value and would repeat exactly the failure the handoff warns about. Against reproducing the 68x observation-compression result on a new corpus: SPIDER already has a valid, audited, real-site cost measurement, and reproducing it changes no decision. The opportunity cost of this direction is that no new dataset enters the program this cycle; given that five consecutive census attempts have not produced one, that cost is low and the information value of a clean external negative is high.

allocation.question: Two bounded external questions, both capable of changing a live SPIDER decision, with a negative as a first-class outcome. (1) CROSS-SITE TRANSFER AS A MEASURABLE QUANTITY: does any published system or benchmark report a cross-site transfer result - mechanisms learned on one set of real websites and executed on a held-out set of never-seen websites - as four separately measurable quantities on a stated denominator (transfer success on a stated N of held-out sites, execution correctness conditional on resolution, abstention-or-refusal rate, and either a stated boilerplate-exclusion rule or an explicit split of task/actionable structure from shared HTML template boilerplate), together with its holdout rule (leave-one-site-out or equivalent, no site-identity leakage) and its denominators; and specifically, does any such report isolate the site-pair-specific stratum from the ubiquitous-template stratum? FALSIFIER: if no source publishes a cross-site transfer rate in that four-part form with a stated holdout split, then C-CROSSSITE has NO external numeric comparator, the registry next_gate must be set internally by whichever lane measures it, and the external-bar question is closed in the negative FOR THAT CORPUS ONLY, with bounded recall over the mandated target list recorded exactly. (2) THE BOUNDING PARAMETERS OF THE WHOLE PRODUCT: what are the exact reported figures, with source, for the routine or delegable recurrence fraction in real computer and agent use, the overhead ratio paid for re-deriving recurrent work, and the compile-versus-reuse build/amortization accounting convention used to report them - because if the delegable fraction is genuinely a small minority of activity, that bounds the entire reachable economic share of SPIDER's product regardless of how good inheritance is, and SPIDER currently has no measured value for it at all; and, separately, whether parametric or compiled memory that survives a backbone change is demonstrated to transfer across models, which would bear on whether SPIDER's inheritance substrate should be retrieval or parameters. MANDATORY ANTI-SELF-FULFILLING-NULL CONTROLS, carrying the fixes this cycle's predecessor exposed: resolve every target name to a verified artifact identity BEFORE scoring any condition and record 'not located' as UNMEASURED and never as a system-level negative (the predecessor's mandated target COVENANT had zero occurrences across all five consulted sources and 1 of 5 was silently substituted by a different system, and the frozen name-to-artifact mapping was crossed); and include a null control with power against the failure that actually occurred, namely inject a deliberately wrong artifact identity or a deliberately shared-boilerplate corpus and require the pipeline to flag it. Do NOT re-run the compiler addressing/regime extraction - that was audited as a source-verified but internally over-claimed packet with mv2 PASS corrected to FAIL and one target UNMEASURED, and repeating it has low marginal value. Do NOT attempt WebGym or WebArena-Infinity deployment as the primary objective: WebGym manifests are recorded UNAVAILABLE pending HF_TOKEN across at least five intel cycles, and if a census is still wanted, record the provisioning status and smallest next action cheaply rather than spending a cycle on it.
allocation.rationale: Intel has a 34-experiment claim streak and 15 of its last 10 on C-CROSSSITE, but the repetition has been in one activity: trying to acquire a task census from WebArena and WebGym. The proposed question is a different activity entirely - whether an external comparator for SPIDER's most central untested claim exists at all - and it has a clean, cheap, decisive falsifier. If no source publishes a four-part cross-site transfer rate on a stated holdout, then the program should stop trying to match one, should set its own holdout rule internally, and the 47 C-CROSSSITE experiments that have failed to produce one become explicable. That is a decision-grade negative obtainable without a browser, docker or a model key. The second question matters more than any other item in the Scout brief: the reported delegable-recurrence fraction and overhead ratio are the only quantities in the entire reconnaissance that would bound SPIDER's product from outside, and if the delegable fraction is around 8 percent then no amount of inheritance quality changes the ceiling. SPIDER has no measured value for it, so intel is the right lane to establish or refute it. Both questions are cheap, both have falsifiers, and both change a decision rather than adding a citation.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: SPIDER's accepted evidence is now large (402 canonical experiments, 10 claims) but shallow in exactly the place that decides the product. Read as a whole, the program has (1) one strong real-Web result that is about OBSERVATION, not inheritance - a minimal HTTP+HTML structural representation at 763 tokens/observation versus 52,020 raw HTML and 50,907 full DOM over 155 observations from 15 eTLD+1 hosts, 68x, paired bootstrap CIs strictly negative (EXP-INTEL-36287179392); (2) a bounded, negative-leaning inheritance result - on the one substrate with a clean span-level endpoint, a no-persistence within-episode scratchpad reaches 1.0000 correctness and closes 100 percent of the residual headroom, but the only arm that amortizes is the unsound one (a state-keyed cache that silently replays 80 wrong actions), and a value-keyed cross-episode cache gets 0 own-mechanism hits by construction, so no sound cross-episode mechanism has ever been shown to amortize (EXP-FRONTIER-36287182510, audit PASS); (3) an UNMEASURED central claim - C-CROSSSITE has 47 experiments and no true website holdout, and its prevalence estimator was shown to be permutation-invariant, so the frozen primary clause reduced to 83.51 > 83.51 and is unevaluable rather than negative; (4) a measurement instrument whose validity contract has failed to certify twice, the second time because the frozen accept branch was arithmetically unreachable and the battery consisted largely of constant statistics (EXP-PHYSICS-36287170603); and (5) an UNMEASURED instrument target - C-LLM-INHERIT and C-PRODUCT-ECON have never been validly run, largely because their comparators had no cost dynamic range. Against that, I verified directly in the shipped product code a fact that reframes the portfolio: src/spider/kernel.py at HEAD is 132 lines, its only distillation path distill() hard-codes confidence=0.5, and resolve() requires confidence >= min_confidence=0.8 while also requiring exact intent string equality. Therefore the shipped kernel cannot turn an observation into an EXECUTABLE inherited mechanism at all, cannot resolve a paraphrased goal, and contains no freshness, repair or verification-rule logic even though the Mechanism model carries those fields. The only test that reaches EXECUTABLE hand-builds a Mechanism at confidence 0.95 and inserts it directly. This independently reproduces SPIDER's own measured finding (0 of 1200 EXECUTABLE resolutions from the committed kernel, EXP-FRONTIER-36249071934) and it explains why C-PARAM-INHERIT, C-LLM-INHERIT, C-PRODUCT-ECON and C-CROSSSITE have all stalled: they were blocked on a capability that is not in the repository. It also means product's parent handoff, which points at src/spider/kernel.py:316-356 and :258 for _build_action_template and _strip_common_prefix, describes a working-tree state that does not exist in the committed 132-line file - uncommitted capability has decayed across many cycles. Consequently this cycle's allocation stops adding synthetic mechanism-scope experiments and instead does four things in parallel: make inheritance executable and durable in the committed kernel with one honestly executed amortized baseline (product); make the inheritance precondition testable on the target domain rather than on another self-authored plan family (frontier, on C-CROSSSITE); certify the measurement instrument, including one real credential-free public-HTTP transfer arm so it is not re-bounded to synthetic middleware (physics); and fix the abstention policy that destroyed a proven selection signal (graph, on C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE). Runtime supplies the two substrate capabilities nothing else in the program has (real 1280x720 Chromium DOM/AX observation, and writable controls), and Intel settles whether any external cross-site transfer comparator exists at all while verifying the specific unverified external numbers that would bound the whole economic premise. C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR are deliberately left unserved this cycle because both are blocked on C-MEAS-VALID, which physics and runtime are now taking; C-WEB-DYNAMICS is left unserved because measuring it again with an uncertified instrument would produce an 82nd uninterpretable result, not because the Physics domain is closed. A recurring control-plane failure mode is visible across three independent packets this cycle - a validity clause unsatisfiable by construction (graph V9), a cost-model ambiguity that flips a headline (frontier 48.00 vs 24.00), and an arithmetically unreachable accept branch (physics) - so every NEW mandate below requires a pre-freeze satisfiability audit of each frozen threshold, clause and validity check against the actual control plane and the packet's own arithmetic. I did not reward any PASS; the two strongest inputs to this cycle were a bounded negative and a verified code defect.
director_mandate.scout_assessment: The brief was treated as staff advice and changed two of six decisions, failed to change two, and supplied one caution that shaped all of them. CHANGED - INTEL: the brief's specific unverified external numbers, above all Activity Frames' reported Routine Overhead Ratio R = 60-343x and delegable-recurrence h = 7.7-9 percent, are the only items in the brief that would bound SPIDER's entire economic premise from outside, and they appear nowhere in SPIDER evidence. I converted them into a verification target for intel rather than a premise, and required artifact-identity resolution before scoring, 'not located' recorded as UNMEASURED, and a null control with power against the failure that actually occurred last cycle (a deliberately wrong artifact identity that the pipeline must flag), because intel's own previous packet recorded a crossed name-to-artifact mapping and one mandated target never located. CHANGED - PHYSICS: the brief is right that 40-plus synthetic C-WEB-DYNAMICS experiments have produced no real-Web evidence, and I turned that into a binding requirement rather than a suggestion - physics' certification contract must demonstrate power on at least one real credential-free public-HTTP condition, so the instrument is not re-bounded to synthetic middleware for a second time. NOT CHANGED - FRONTIER: the brief offered both 'accept the handoff' and 'park the synthetic residual-novelty program and test on real task families'. I rejected the first on information-content grounds - the proposed POSITIVE arm plants a stable readable identifier in the response body, so it cannot fail, and the NULL arm plants its absence, so it cannot succeed, on the same self-authored plan family and the same stdlib substrate, with abstract units and no model call - and took the second, sharpening it into a real-website holdout with a measured identifier-prevalence term that can decide SPIDER's replay architecture. The brief's own executive assessment supports this ('Frontier lane has 11-claim streak with tunnel_flag=true, indicating deep local trapping'). NOT CHANGED - PRODUCT: the brief's top product suggestion, C-LLM-INHERIT on WebGym OOD tasks, cannot be executed and would not be informative if it could. It presupposes a working shipped kernel; the committed kernel cannot execute an inherited mechanism at all. It also depends on WebGym, which SPIDER evidence records as HF_TOKEN-blocked across at least five intel cycles (EXP-INTEL-36042590671, 36058324385, 36084509510, 36092351694, 36095582115) while the brief presents WebGym as available infrastructure. NOT CHANGED - RUNTIME: the brief's Keycloak/OIDC plus CDN-robustness recommendation adds unprovisioned infrastructure and does not unblock any currently live decision; the live Runtime blocker is the write leg and the transport boundary. CAUTION APPLIED THROUGHOUT: the brief's external section is unverified, and at least one of its figures is numerically adjacent to a number SPIDER measured independently (its '86x compression' against SPIDER's audited 68x), and its arXiv identifiers are used in a pattern that previously caused intel a name-to-artifact crossing (spec 'TraceCompiler' mapped to arXiv:2608.02680, which is a different system). I therefore treated every external finding as a prior to be tested and none as evidence, and I did not let the brief's WebGym or WebArena-Infinity availability claims override the documented provisioning blocks.

inherited_last_verdict: MIXED_COST_ESTABLISHED_PREVALENCE_UNEVALUABLE_CROSSSITE_HELD_AT_HYPOTHESIS_NO_PROMOTION: the measurement transaction completed validly and credential-free (result.json status=COMPLETE, outcome=MIXED; audit.json status=REVISE, producer_claim_supported=true), and it settles exactly one of the two halves the mandate asked for. COST HALF ESTABLISHED at the audited ceiling: a minimal HTTP+HTML structural representation costs 763.06 tokens / 2,801.19 bytes per observation (mean; median 576 / 2,138) over n=155 observations from 15 eTLD+1 hosts, against B-RAW-HTML 52,020.35 / 151,741.41, B-FULL-DOM 50,907.34 / 145,140.82 and the preregistered B-A11Y-TREE approximation 16,793.67 / 48,693.05, all four on the same 155 observations under one shared tokenizer (cl100k_base, n_vocab 100277); ratios 68.2x / 66.7x / 22.0x in tokens, with paired eTLD+1-level bootstrap (10,000 replicates) 95% CI upper bounds of -22,823.81 tokens vs full DOM and -8,932.25 tokens vs a11y, both strictly negative, and minimal smaller on 155/155 and 150/155 observations respectively. The frozen cost clause is SATISFIED (audit baseline_findings[0..3], recomputed_metrics.cost_per_observation_mean and cost_paired_differences). PREVALENCE HALF NOT ESTABLISHED AND NOT FALSIFIED: the frozen primary clause is UNEVALUABLE because the frozen estimator and its frozen null are the same object up to a label. AGF = sum_K (T_K^2 - sum_s n_{s,K}^2)/(2*total_signatures) depends on the per-host key counts only through the symmetric quantity sum_s n_{s,K}^2, so permuting eTLD+1 labels is exactly invariant: 1,000 permutations produced exactly 1 distinct value, bitwise equal to the observed point estimate 83.51083467094703, std = 0.0 exactly, and the clause reduces to 83.51083467094703 > 83.51083467094703. result.json records primary_evaluable=false and primary_satisfied=null, NOT false, and the auditor confirms this (audit required_fixes[0], validity_findings[0]-[1]). This is a defect in the frozen estimator/null pair, not infrastructure failure and not a scientific negative: no substrate was missing, 0 of 155 pages failed extraction, and 0 credentials, registry pulls, browser binaries or model API calls were used (audit validity_findings[2]). C-CROSSSITE therefore stays at HYPOTHESIS. The frozen design's own consequence (prereg.md section 18) ties the HYPOTHESIS->EXPERIMENTAL move to 'measured prevalence AND cost floor'; only cost was measured, and the registry construct is mechanism transfer across a website holdout (next_gate 'true website holdout without site identity leakage'), which this packet did not measure, so promoting the claim would be status inflation. audit.json status is REVISE, not PASS, so VALIDATED is unavailable in any case, and lane=intel forecloses PRODUCT_CORE. No product action, no promotion, continue=false. The one genuinely decision-relevant prevalence datum is NOT the AGF magnitude but the audit's decomposition: only 67 distinct signature keys are shared by >=2 of the 15 hosts, list signatures are 97.25% of all 416,218 matched instances, a single key list(ul, /{slug}/{slug}) is 49.56% of them, 96.49% come from keys carried by 6+ hosts, and only 3.51% from the site-pair-specific 2-5-host regime a cross-site inheritance product would monetise; the audit's own words are that the frozen AGF 'primarily measures that the Web is built from <ul> elements, not that it contains reusable task structure'. Under the only non-frozen null with power (NC-SIG-REASSIGN, 869 distinct values, std 0.193) the observed sharing sits 18.58 AGF units and 0.2507 Jaccard units BELOW a random re-partition of the same template vocabulary. That is evidence against the specific mechanism this statistic can see; it is explicitly NOT a bounded negative on C-CROSSSITE, because the statistic cannot separate reusable task structure from shared HTML boilerplate, and the auditor reserved independent confirmation of that producer-constructed randomisation before any lane re-scopes on its direction (audit unresolved[3]). Five of twenty pre-registered hosts are recorded NOT_MEASURED with exact blocking artefacts per portfolio directive G1, and are neither negatives nor evidence about those sites.
inherited_next_question: Does any published system or benchmark report a CROSS-SITE TRANSFER result - mechanisms learned on one set of real websites and then executed on a held-out set of never-seen websites - as four separately measurable quantities on a stated denominator (transfer success on a stated N of held-out sites, execution correctness conditional on resolution, abstention-or-refusal rate, and either a stated boilerplate-exclusion rule or an explicit split of task/actionable structure from shared HTML template boilerplate), together with its holdout rule (leave-one-site-out or equivalent, no site-identity leakage) and its denominators; and specifically, does any such report isolate the site-pair-specific stratum from the ubiquitous-template stratum? FALSIFIER: no source publishes a cross-site transfer rate in that four-part form with a stated holdout split, in which case C-CROSSSITE has NO external numeric comparator, the registry next_gate 'true website holdout without site identity leakage' must be set internally, and the external-bar question is closed in the negative FOR THAT CORPUS ONLY, with bounded recall over the mandate's target list recorded exactly. A negative is worth having only if the search can actually fail, so the design must carry the fixes this cycle and its predecessor exposed rather than repeating a self-fulfilling null: (i) resolve every target name to a verified artifact identity BEFORE scoring any condition, and record 'not located' as UNMEASURED and never as a system-level negative - that single omission is exactly how the predecessor's mandated target COVENANT, 1 of 5, was silently substituted by arXiv:2608.02680 and lost; (ii) include a null control with power against the failure that actually occurred, i.e. inject a deliberately wrong artifact identity or a deliberately shared-boilerplate corpus and require the pipeline to flag it, since the predecessor's NC-FABRICATED-BINDING-CLAIMS searched for three literal phrases no paper would contain and detected nothing while a target identity was being substituted underneath it; (iii) require every reported number to carry its accounting convention, its denominator and its holdout rule, so that a corpus figure cannot be mistaken for a rate. CONTINGENCY IF NEGATIVE, recorded here as routing rather than as a second question: C-CROSSSITE's internal bar must then be set by a statistic that is NOT invariant to host relabelling paired with a null built on a permutation that IS - the frozen AGF here is provably invariant under eTLD+1 relabelling, 1 distinct value over 1,000 permutations bitwise equal to the point estimate - and that statistic must partition shared HTML template boilerplate from site-pair-specific task structure, because on this packet's 155 pages 97.25% of matched instances were list signatures and only 3.51% came from the site-pair-specific 2-5-host regime a cross-site inheritance product would monetise. That internal work belongs to C-CROSSSITE's owner lanes (physics, graph, frontier), not to Intel.
